A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ERG research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, were readable and could be matched across revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original COCO and ImageNet generation experiments, guidance comparisons, ablations and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds FID-tuned comparisons, public-model evaluations and repeated-seed DiT results.

M1.justification: The attention rectification updates, I-ERG/C-ERG combination, kickoff threshold and guidance equation are retained. Both implementation listings are unchanged apart from formatting. Additional architecture evaluations do not establish a new algorithm or adaptation.

E1.justification: The explicit experimental descriptions retain COCO, ImageNet and the same generation tasks; additional architectures change model settings. However, v2 Table 14 newly lists CC12M among assets used without explaining its role in training or evaluation. Whether this represents additional dataset coverage is unresolved.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained main experiments is unchanged. v2 adds a comparison against baseline EDM2 and EDM2 with AutoGuidance in Table 11, extending AutoGuidance to this setting. The newly cited CFG++ is not an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: v2 adds FID-only hyperparameter selection, sFID/IS and DINOv2-FID evaluation, and experiments using additional public architectures and the official DiT evaluation setup. The component ablation changes its stated final control from alpha reweighting to gamma step size, and Table 7 revises the reported SD3 text encoder. These are new or revised reported settings, without establishing reruns of retained experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix D.6 adds an analysis of whether ERG remains competitive when every method is optimized for FID alone. Existing velocity, attention-layer and kickoff-threshold analyses remain. The component ablation is revised, while Figure 4 removes the precision and recall temperature-sensitivity panels.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix G and Table 13 introduce aggregate results over ten random seeds, with mean-plus/minus values and minimum–maximum ranges for five DiT metrics. v1 has seed-based illustrations and an initial-noise variance analysis, but no comparable repeated-evaluation uncertainty reporting. This is newly reported statistical evidence, not an established increase from a known earlier run count; some reported ranges are inconsistent.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial numerical evidence, including FID-tuned results of 4.93 for ERG versus 5.25 for CFG, additional metrics, and public-model comparisons. These are additional settings, not same-setting improvements over v1. Common main-table values remain unchanged, with text-to-image precision/recall relocated to Table 9; corresponding metrics disappear from several other comparisons. The multistep table also contains numerical revisions beyond reformatting.

T1.justification: New Appendix C develops an exponential-reweighting and KL-regularized optimization interpretation of I-ERG, plus a first-order Taylor/Jacobian derivation for C-ERG. These substantive mathematical arguments are absent from v1. The existing Hopfield formulation is largely retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: inference-time attention rectification, improved quality/diversity/consistency trade-offs, conditional and unconditional applicability, and compatibility with APG/CADS. Rewording and additional supporting experiments do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds reward-based and semantic-sensitivity interpretations, explicit architecture/depth limitations, and discussion of FID optimization and seed stability. These substantially extend v1's attention/velocity explanations. However, Appendix B's statement that testing covered only diffusion transformers conflicts with the new U-Net evaluations in Appendix G.

D1.justification: v2 expands the sampling-parameter table, identifies evaluation libraries for additional public models, and adds dataset/model/library links in Table 14. Core pseudocode and most existing defaults remain unchanged. Two parameter configurations are both labeled SD3-medium, leaving the added configuration's model assignment unclear.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to CFG++ and YFCC100M and removes the 2019 improved precision/recall reference. Positioning relative to CFG, SEG, AutoGuidance, APG and CADS remains substantially unchanged. Publication-metadata updates do not constitute new related work.

P1.justification: v2 extensively edits prose and reorganizes the appendices. Its method structure also introduces substantial duplication: Sections 3 and 4 repeat the introduction, and Sections 4.4–4.6 repeat the three subsections in 4.1–4.3. This materially changes document structure without changing the method.

P2.justification: Multiple tables are redesigned, split or relocated, including moving Table 1's precision/recall into an appendix table and restructuring the ablation tables. Figure 4 changes from six panels to four, Figure 19 gains SD3.5 examples, and new evaluation, statistics and asset tables substantially expand the displays. Most existing qualitative image grids are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful public-model validation, FID-focused analysis, explicit limitations and repeated-seed reporting. However, duplicated method sections impair clarity, Table 13 reports a baseline IS mean of 278.67 outside its stated range of 270.67–273.39, and Appendix C's reward definition does not match the ratio preceding its integration. These problems weaken the new statistical and theoretical support, leaving the net quality benefit uncertain.
